name: Xiamen
title: Xiamen Ship Thickness Measurement | Fujian Coast UTM
description: UTM in Xiamen for container ships, bulk carriers and ro-ro ships on the Fujian coast: hull structure and ballast tank gauging, plus pre-docking work.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships in Xiamen
intro: Xiamen is the main container port of Fujian province, on the western side of the Taiwan Strait. Its terminals around Xiamen Bay serve intra-Asia, Southeast Asian and long-haul container services, alongside bulk carriers, ro-ro ships and cruise calls. Short-sea ships calling here wear hard and stay briefly, so gauging is often spread over several calls, an anchorage wait or a docking further along the Fujian coast. The team comes from India for each job, and its timing allows for typhoons and the winter monsoon.
keywords: ultrasonic thickness gauging for ships in xiamen

highlights.h: Ballast tank gauging split across calls
highlights.p: Feeders on tight rotations rarely open every tank in one stay. Dividing the tanks into groups that fit each Xiamen call, and combining the readings afterwards, completes the scope before the survey without extra off-hire.

Frequent ballast changes, cargo handling at every port and a warm, humid climate keep corrosion active in ballast tanks, hold structure and deck fittings. Measurement points are placed where that wear concentrates.

Typhoons in summer and autumn and the strong north-east monsoon through the strait in winter can both interrupt launch work. Anchorage jobs at those times are planned with slack and with the critical tanks listed first.

port.h: Xiamen: Fujian's container port on the Taiwan Strait
p: Xiamen's harbour is a sheltered bay around Xiamen Island, with container terminals spread around the bay, including the Haicang area on the mainland shore, and a cruise terminal on the island itself. It is the province's principal container gateway. Container lines link Xiamen with the rest of the China coast, Southeast Asia and long-haul markets, and the port also handles bulk cargo, project cargo and vehicles. Shipping across the strait connects the city with Taiwan, and coastal services run north and south along the Fujian shore.

The ships are a mix typical of a large regional port: feeders and intra-Asia container ships on busy rotations, mid-sized bulk carriers bringing coal and other raw materials to the Fujian coast, ro-ro ships and car carriers, and coastal cargo ships. Warm, humid conditions and short-sea rotations with frequent ballasting keep corrosion active in ballast tanks, void spaces and deck piping, and these ships see more cargo handling per year than a deep-sea bulk carrier ever does. A Xiamen call is often short, but anchorage waits in the bay and its approaches give longer windows for gauging ships in ballast.

Shipbuilding and repair are part of the bay too. Xiamen Shipbuilding Industry is known in particular for car carriers, and repair facilities around the bay and along the Fujian coast take ships for docking. For owners of feeder and short-sea fleets that trade constantly along the China coast, Xiamen can be a convenient place to dock, with pre-docking gauging done during a preceding Xiamen call; the readings are most useful when the next dock is only a short coastal passage away and there is no time to measure at sea. The weather sets its own calendar: typhoons in summer and autumn, and strong north-east monsoon winds through the Taiwan Strait in winter, can interrupt anchorage and launch work and need to be allowed for in any schedule.

facilities.h: Berths, anchorages and yards around Xiamen Bay
p: Xiamen work is done alongside or at anchor far more often than in dock. The container terminals at Haicang give access to deck structure, coamings and piping on container ships, and to ballast tanks when the ship's stay and ballast plan allow. Bulk berths around the bay allow hold gauging after discharge, while ro-ro ships release their vehicle decks as cargo moves. At anchorage, ships waiting in ballast can open holds and tanks for pre-purchase, on-hire or pre-docking gauging, with the team boarding by launch arranged through the agent. Inside the bay the water is sheltered, so outside the monsoon and typhoon periods launch transfers to ships at anchor are usually straightforward.

Docking work takes place in the repair yards around Xiamen and elsewhere on the Fujian coast. For short-sea and feeder owners, the value of a Xiamen gauging often lies in the sequence: readings taken at berth or anchorage define the steel renewal scope, the yard prepares accordingly, and the survey gauging in dock then confirms and completes the picture. Ships that trade between Xiamen and the Pearl River Delta can equally carry the Xiamen readings to a yard further south.
list: Haicang container terminals — container berths on the mainland side of the bay; deck, coaming and scrubber discharge lines, plus ballast tanks when the stay and ballast plan allow.
Bulk and general cargo berths around the bay — coal and raw-material carriers of handy and Supramax size; hold plating, hopper slopes and hatch covers once discharge ends.
Xiamen Bay anchorages — sheltered water for launch boarding outside the typhoon and monsoon periods; ships in ballast measured ahead of a sale, a charter or a yard visit.
Ro-ro berths — car deck, ramp and stern door gauging on ro-ro ships and car carriers as decks become free during cargo work.
Fujian coast repair yards — dockings for short-sea and feeder owners, with renewal survey gauging and re-measurement of steel the yard has replaced.

context.h: Coastal rules and short-sea trading in Fujian
p: Foreign ships at Xiamen are inspected under the Tokyo MoU by China's Maritime Safety Administration, and the Fujian coast is inside China's domestic emission control arrangements, which also limit where open-loop scrubbers may discharge. Smaller feeder and short-sea ships seldom carry scrubbers at all, so their inspection needs centre on hull structure, tanks and piping rather than exhaust-cleaning systems; the larger container ships calling at Haicang are where scrubber piping becomes part of the scope.

Short-sea trading is hard on ships in ways that reward regular gauging. Frequent port calls and ballast changes, cargo handling at every stop and a warm, humid climate all speed up corrosion in ballast tanks, hold structure and deck fittings. Ships in the trade between Fujian, the rest of the China coast and Southeast Asia also face scrutiny from charterers and port state inspectors, who look closely at hatch covers, ballast tank coatings and fire main condition. Feeder ship thickness measurement between surveys lets the owner plan steel and piping renewal into the next docking instead of reacting to a deficiency raised at the gangway.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Xiamen
jobs.p: Ship inspection in Xiamen is usually built around a short-sea or feeder ship's regular call, an anchorage wait, or a docking on the Fujian coast. We fix the scope with the superintendent beforehand, mobilise the team from India for the confirmed window, and keep a margin in the plan during the typhoon and winter monsoon seasons. Earlier TM reports, where the owner has them, are used to place the measurement points.
list: Ballast tank gauging on a feeder container ship split across two Xiamen calls, so the full tank scope is complete before its intermediate survey.
After discharge at a Xiamen bulk berth, a Supramax's holds and hatch covers measured and its hatch corners crack-tested, ahead of a charterer's hold inspection.
A short-sea ship anchored off Xiamen before heading to a Fujian yard: ballast tanks and holds measured so the steel list for its renewal survey is ready on arrival.
A ro-ro ship's car decks, ramps and stern door measured during its Xiamen call, with each deck released by the chief officer as the vehicles move off.
Delivery into a time charter at Xiamen: a bulk carrier's holds and tanks measured so that owner and charterer start the charter with a shared condition record.

logistics: Arrival is at Xiamen Gaoqi International Airport — or the new Xiang'an airport once it takes over from Gaoqi — normally via a Chinese or Southeast Asian hub. The ship's agent obtains passes for Haicang and the other port areas and books the launch for any anchorage boarding, weather permitting. For an India-based team, the Chinese business visa and its supporting invitation letter are the step that needs most notice, so applications are made as soon as the berth, anchorage window or dock date is fixed.

faqs.q: Can ballast tank gauging on a feeder be split over several Xiamen calls?
faqs.a: Yes, and on tight rotations it is often the only practical way. We divide the tanks into groups that can each be ventilated, entered and gauged within one call, record exactly what has been covered, and complete the rest at following calls. The readings are then combined into one report on the TM formats ahead of the survey.

faqs.q: Does the winter monsoon in the Taiwan Strait affect anchorage work?
faqs.a: It can. Strong north-easterly winds through the strait in winter, like typhoons in summer and autumn, make launch transfers difficult and sometimes stop them. Berth and yard work is less affected. When a Xiamen job falls in either season, we agree priorities with the superintendent so the most important spaces are gauged first.

faqs.q: Where does corrosion concentrate on short-sea ships trading from Xiamen?
faqs.a: Ballast tanks are the first concern, particularly where coating has broken down on the upper side shell and bulkheads, and at stiffener edges and welds. Hold frames and hatch coamings suffer from cargo handling at frequent calls, and deck piping and air pipe heads waste in the humid, salty air. We place measurement points to capture those areas as well as the minimum the survey requires.

faqs.q: Can gauging done in Xiamen be used when the ship docks elsewhere?
faqs.a: Yes. Hull gauging in Xiamen, whether at a berth or at anchorage, is recorded against the ship's structural drawings and the TM report layout, so the yard and the class surveyor at the docking port can use them for planning. Where the docking is in a Fujian or Pearl River Delta yard, the same team can follow the ship and complete the survey gauging in dock.
